I'd just returned from an overseas tour and a friend had picked me up at the pier with my car. I drove him back to his house and saw the lady who would become my wife walking down the steps with his wife.

That was it.

Honestly, its hard to say. My wife and I have been through a lot and we started dating at 13, now 27. Since then he have both gone to college (different schools in different states), lived together far away from our home town, both worked full time, attempted to break up, and recently had a baby.

There is a lot of pressure that comes from others in our situation. People have honestly told us "if you two break up I will lose all faith in love". A couple years back I started to question everything. I wondered if what we had was love or if we were just comfortable with eachother. Neither of us had ever been with another person and that really weighted on my mind, how can we know this is it? It was a rough time for me and one day I told her how I felt, broke up with her and she packed a bag and went to her mom's. The next few days were spent in heavy contemplation. I didn't talk at work and I cried a lot at home. Despite me telling her not to call me, she rang me and said she wanted to see what was going on. She pulled up to the house and we just sat in the car and talked, that conversation changed my mind. Here I was, trying to end an 11 year old relationship and she was perfectly calm and caring. She knew she might leave that car without me and she talked to me like an adult. She wasn't overly emotional, we just spilled out guts in that car and got to the bottom of the problem.

In that moment I knew she was perfect for me and I couldn't live in doubt any longer. That year I proposed to her, the following year we were married, and now we have a hansom son together. I love this woman so much and I regret nothing.
The first day I met her. In fact, I told my best friend I was going to marry her. He laughed it off, then went out on a date with her. I was crushed. Almost 20 years later. Here we are.
